accepted.s: The National Council for Science & Technology Communication (NCSTC) functions under which organisation?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
accepted.x: NCSTC is organised under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

o: Understanding Ecosystem for Health and Well-being
Science and Technology for Rural Transformation
accepted.x: The theme of the 31st National Children’s Science Congress was “Understanding Ecosystem for Health and Well-being.”

accepted.s: ‘Science on Wheels’ mobile laboratories, including those operating in Alluri Sitharama Raju district, are associated with which body?
o: National Council for Science & Technology Communication
accepted.x: The ‘Science on Wheels’ mobile laboratories are an NCSTC initiative; the programme also includes Alluri Sitharama Raju district in Andhra Pradesh.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM):
1. It is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Culture.
2. It was formed on 4 April 1978.
3. Its headquarters is located in Kolkata.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. NCSM is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Culture, formed on 4 April 1978, with headquarters at Kolkata.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional detail separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Council of Science Museums?
o: It administers 49 innovation hubs and is headquartered at New Delhi.
It operates only mobile laboratories under the Department of Science and Technology.
It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Education established in 2015.
It administers a network of 26 science cities, centres and museums and is described as the world’s largest network of science centres under one administrative umbrella.
accepted.x: NCSM has 26 science cities, centres and museums and is regarded as the world’s largest network of science centres under one administrative umbrella.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the scale and administrative character of NCSM from those of other outreach programmes.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: How many Mobile Science Exhibition buses were associated with the National Council of Science Museums in IYB 2026?
accepted.x: NCSM had 46 Mobile Science Exhibition buses in IYB 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate closely placed numerical figures by linking the number to the specific programme.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: The National Council of Science Museums is the nodal agency for which scheme of the Ministry of Culture?
o: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science
accepted.x: NCSM is the nodal agency for the Ministry of Culture’s Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science (SPoCS).
accepted.tq: Identify the nodal agency by matching the body with the exact scheme name.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science, which of the following correctly represents the reported infrastructure?
accepted.x: SPoCS has resulted in the setting up of 26 science centres and 49 innovation hubs.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing paired figures in a comparison-based numerical question.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Which set of places was reported to have three additional innovation hubs ready under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science?
accepted.x: The three additional innovation hubs ready under SPoCS were located at Warangal, Jodhpur and Udaipur.
accepted.tq: Use the complete place-list rather than recognising only one familiar location.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about NCSM’s institutional structure:
1. Its Central Research & Training Laboratory is located in Kolkata.
2. It has national, regional and sub-regional centres.
3. It functions exclusively through state-level centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. NCSM has its Central Research & Training Laboratory at Kolkata and follows a three-tier national, regional and sub-regional structure; it does not function exclusively through state-level centres.
accepted.tq: Find the single over-restrictive statement containing ‘exclusively’.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Vigyan Rail, described as a science exhibition on wheels, was launched during which period?
accepted.x: Vigyan Rail was a science exhibition on wheels associated with the Department of Science and Technology during 2003–04.
accepted.tq: Differentiate nearby outreach exhibitions by their launch period.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Science Express?
o: It was a mobile laboratory of NCSM first launched in 1978.
It was a school programme of the Ministry of Education launched in 2015.
It was a science exhibition on wheels organised by CSIR in 2003–04.
It was an exhibition train of DST with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad, first flagged off in 2007.
accepted.x: Science Express was organised by DST with the Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre, Ahmedabad, and was first flagged off in 2007.
accepted.tq: Use the organiser-partner-year combination to reject swapped institutional descriptions.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: The later thematic versions of Science Express included which of the following?
o: Biodiversity Special and Climate Action Special
Health Innovation Special and Space Science Special
Children’s Science Special and Agriculture Special
Ecosystem Special and Rural Technology Special
accepted.x: The later thematic versions of Science Express included the Biodiversity Special and the Climate Action Special.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact titles of thematic extensions rather than the general exhibition name.

accepted.s: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 under which ministry and with what broad purpose?
o: Ministry of Earth Sciences, to teach climate science through exhibitions
Ministry of Culture, to establish science museums in every district
Department of Science and Technology, to operate mobile science buses
Ministry of Education, to promote practical and inquiry-based learning of science and mathematics in schools
accepted.x: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of HRD, now the Ministry of Education, to encourage practical and inquiry-based science and mathematics learning in schools.
accepted.tq: Combine the launch year, ministry and purpose instead of relying on the programme name alone.
accepted.sec: Science outreach bodies and exhibitions → organiser

accepted.s: Which institution trains teachers under the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan?
o: Vikram A. Sarabhai Community Science Centre
National Council of Science Museums, Kolkata
accepted.x: IISER Tirupati trains teachers under the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution linked to implementation rather than the ministry that launched the programme.

Match List-I with List-II:

accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Indian science academies in chronological order of their founding:
A. INSA
B. NASI
C. IASc

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NASI was founded in 1930, IASc in 1934 and INSA in 1935. Therefore, the order is B, C, A.
accepted.tq: Use the first and last founding years to establish the sequence before checking the middle item.
accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences. C. V. Raman founded IASc in 1934, while INSA was founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India.
accepted.tq: Check both the founder and founding year in each pair to catch swapped identities.
accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s: The Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc) was founded by whom and is headquartered where?
accepted.x: IASc was founded by C. V. Raman in 1934 and is headquartered at Bengaluru.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two prominent founder-academy associations.
accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian National Science Academy (INSA):
1. It was founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India.
2. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
3. It was renamed INSA in 1970.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. INSA originated as the National Institute of Sciences of India in 1935, is headquartered at New Delhi and adopted the name INSA in 1970.
accepted.tq: Verify the institutional origin, location and later renaming as separate factual elements.
accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with NASI?
o: Founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and regarded as the oldest Indian science academy
Founded in 1935 as the National Institute of Sciences of India at New Delhi
Renamed in 1970 after being founded by C. V. Raman
Founded in 1934 by C. V. Raman at Bengaluru
accepted.x: NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and is regarded as the oldest science academy in India.
accepted.tq: Combine origin, founder and relative status to distinguish similar academies.
accepted.sec: Science academies → headquarters, founder, founding year

accepted.s: The India International Science Festival (IISF) is best described by which of the following statements?
o: An annual festival begun in 2015 in New Delhi, organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati
An annual exhibition organised by NCSM under the Ministry of Culture since 1978
A school science congress organised by the Ministry of Education since 2015
A biennial festival begun in 2007 by DST alone
accepted.x: IISF began in 2015 in New Delhi and is organised by the Ministry of Science & Technology and the Ministry of Earth Sciences with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA).
accepted.tq: Match the festival with its start year, place and complete group of organisers.
accepted.sec: Popular science awards and forums - India International Science Festival (IISF)
